astro.notes: Ships near-zero JS by default. Islands architecture hydrates only interactive components. Cloudflare acquired Astro Technology Company Jan 2026; Astro 6 beta runs on workerd runtime. MIT license maintained. Lighthouse SEO 100 achievable out of box. Best for content-first, read-heavy sites.
astro.responsive_grid: Tailwind CSS recommended — no built-in grid but integrates trivially
astro.dev_velocity: HIGH — large template ecosystem, clean HTML output, minimal config
weaknesses: Not ideal for heavily dynamic apps
astro.2026_status: fastest-growing framework for content sites as of Feb 2026

nextjs.notes: Next.js 15+ with Server Actions makes Stripe Embedded Checkout trivial — PCI offloaded to Stripe, no card data touches your server. React 19 integration. App Router is now stable. Best for restaurant online ordering + menu management + Stripe/Square payment flows. NextMerce and Medusa are production-ready e-commerce starters.
nextjs.responsive_grid: Tailwind CSS first-class; CSS Modules supported
nextjs.dev_velocity: HIGH — massive ecosystem, Vercel tight integration
nextjs.stripe_integration: Embedded Checkout recommended 2026 — iframe on your domain, full PCI compliance delegated
weaknesses: Vercel vendor lock-in risk on advanced features
nextjs.2026_status: dominant for dynamic SMB apps; slightly losing static site share to Astro

sveltekit.notes: Svelte 5 runtime is 1.6 KB vs React 42 KB. Svelte Runes (fine-grained reactivity) replace stores — cleaner real-time patterns. Excellent for client portals needing reactive UI without heavy framework overhead. WebSocket and SSE integration is idiomatic. Smallest practical bundles of any full-stack framework.
sveltekit.responsive_grid: Tailwind CSS recommended; no built-in grid
sveltekit.dev_velocity: MEDIUM-HIGH — gentler learning curve than React, smaller ecosystem
sveltekit.2026_status: rising — Svelte 5 Runes adoption accelerating; strong for portal use cases

react_vite.notes: Pure React SPA (Vite) suits pharmacy workflow tools where SEO is irrelevant (authenticated portals). Not recommended for public-facing brochure sites. Combine with React Query for server state, Zustand for local state. For public-facing pharmacy pages, wrap in Next.js or use Astro for the marketing shell.
react_vite.dev_velocity: HIGH — largest ecosystem, most hiring pool

angular.notes: Angular Signals (v17+) add fine-grained reactivity. Best when team is already Angular-trained. Overkill for typical 5-page SMB sites. Strong opinionated structure suits law firms with in-house dev teams. Angular Material has strong responsive grid (CSS Grid + Flex). Not recommended for new SMB template systems unless enterprise client base.
angular.responsive_grid: Angular Material CDK Layout — built-in responsive breakpoints
angular.dev_velocity: LOW-MEDIUM for small teams — steep learning curve, high boilerplate

nuxt.notes: Nuxt 4 + Nitro engine. Vue 4 Vapor Mode (fine-grained reactivity, no vDOM diffing) landing in 2026. Good for teams already in Vue. Nuxt Content module makes restaurant menu/blog management easy. Not worth switching to from Next.js unless team has Vue preference.
nuxt.responsive_grid: Tailwind CSS; Nuxt UI component library has responsive primitives
weaknesses: Smaller US market share than React ecosystem

automation_tools.name: Plop
automation_tools.use_case: Component and page scaffolding within an existing project. Generate new client site from template: run `plop client` → prompts for business name, type, color scheme → creates pages, components, config files. Low overhead, stays in project.
automation_tools.best_for: Per-project file generation; CI-integrated component generation

automation_tools.name: Yeoman
automation_tools.use_case: Full project scaffolding from generator. Write a yo generator once that creates the full client site structure: `yo smb-template --type restaurant`. Handles deps, test setup, config. Older but battle-tested.
automation_tools.best_for: Greenfield project scaffolding from a master template
automation_tools.maturity: MATURE — reduced velocity since 2022 but stable
automation_tools.verdict: ACCEPTABLE but consider custom scripts or Turborepo for new template systems

automation_tools.name: Custom Bash/Node Scripts
automation_tools.use_case: For agencies: a single `create-client.sh` or `create-client.js` that: (1) clones template repo, (2) replaces tokens (business name, colors, phone, address), (3) creates git repo, (4) pushes to GitHub, (5) triggers Netlify/Vercel deploy hook. Full control, zero external dependency.
automation_tools.best_for: Agency workflows with standardized client types
automation_tools.verdict: RECOMMENDED for production agency workflow — combine with Plop for component level

automation_tools.name: Turborepo
automation_tools.use_case: Monorepo management when agency maintains 10+ client sites. Shared component library in packages/ui. Each client site imports from shared lib. Incremental builds — only rebuild changed sites.
automation_tools.best_for: Multi-client monorepo where sites share component library

automation_tools.name: Nx
automation_tools.use_case: Alternative to Turborepo for monorepo. More opinionated, stronger code generation (nx generate). Better for Angular or mixed-framework monorepos.
automation_tools.verdict: USE if Angular is primary framework; prefer Turborepo otherwise

automation_tools.name: WordPress + WP-CLI + Bedrock
automation_tools.use_case: For agencies with non-technical clients who need CMS access. Automate: `wp-cli` core install + theme + plugins via shell script. Bedrock adds composer-based dependency management.
automation_tools.best_for: Non-technical clients who will manage their own content
automation_tools.verdict: VALID for non-technical SMB clients; not recommended for performance-critical sites

recommended_steps: 1. Intake form (Typeform/Tally) → captures: business name, type, colors, logo, contact info, social links
2. Automated script clones template repo for vertical (contractor/restaurant/pharmacy/lawyer)
4. GitHub repo created (gh CLI), Netlify/Vercel project linked via API
5. DNS instructions emailed to client (Netlify DNS or Cloudflare)
6. Preview URL sent to client in <15 minutes of intake form submission
7. Revision loop via GitHub PR — client sees live preview per PR
8. Domain connected, SSL auto-provisioned, monitoring set up (BetterUptime free)
client_onboarding_workflow.notes: Key insight from 2026 research: agencies save most time not in build but in DNS + content iteration. Build a CMS layer (Decap CMS or Keystatic) so clients can update content without opening tickets.

pharmacy_backend_options.cost: free tier (500 DBs, 9GB storage, 1B row reads/month)
pharmacy_backend_options.notes: Local-first SQLite + cloud sync. Embedded replicas = zero-latency reads. Privacy-first by design — data can stay on-device. For pharmacy: patient refill requests stay local, sync to primary only when online. BAA not currently offered by Turso — use for small independent pharmacies where HIPAA-lite approach is acceptable. Encryption at rest via libsql encryption extension.
pharmacy_backend_options.verdict: BEST for independent pharmacy, local-first model
pharmacy_backend_options.encryption: at-rest via libsql extension; in-transit TLS

pharmacy_backend_options.cost: free tier (0.5 GB storage, 100 compute hours/month)
pharmacy_backend_options.notes: Serverless Postgres with branching. Scale-to-zero means no idle cost for SMB pharmacies. Postgres means standard HIPAA tech safeguards apply. No BAA on free tier. Paid plans include BAA option. Strong for prescription tracking with relational integrity.
pharmacy_backend_options.verdict: BEST for pharmacy needing relational integrity + Postgres ecosystem

pharmacy_backend_options.notes: MySQL-compatible, horizontal scaling. HIPAA compliance documentation available. BAA on Enterprise. More expensive than alternatives for SMB use.
pharmacy_backend_options.verdict: OVERKILL for independent pharmacy — use for chain pharmacies at scale

pharmacy_backend_options.notes: SQLite file on server + Litestream streams WAL to S3/R2 continuously. Zero replication lag. Single-server model — fine for independent pharmacy. Full control of data, no third-party BAA needed (you own the infrastructure). Encrypt SQLite at rest via SQLCipher.
pharmacy_backend_options.verdict: BEST for self-hosted independent pharmacy — maximum privacy control, near-zero cost
pharmacy_backend_options.encryption: SQLCipher for at-rest; TLS for in-transit

pharmacy_privacy_patterns.spa_architecture: Static frontend (Astro marketing page) + SvelteKit authenticated portal. Marketing page = public, zero patient data. Portal = authenticated SPA behind Cloudflare Access or auth middleware.
pharmacy_privacy_patterns.auth_recommendation: Clerk or Auth.js (Next.js) / Lucia (SvelteKit) — session tokens only, no patient data in JWT
prescription_refill_workflow: 1. Patient authenticates (Clerk/Lucia — session cookie, no PHI in token)
2. Patient selects medication from their profile (loaded from DB on server-side only)
3. Refill request written to DB with status=PENDING, timestamped
4. Pharmacist dashboard shows PENDING queue (server-side rendered, no client-side PHI exposure)
5. Pharmacist approves → status=APPROVED → SMS/email notification via Twilio/Resend
6. Patient sees status update on next portal visit
pharmacy_privacy_patterns.critical_rule: Role separation at DB level — patients query only their own records via user_id FK constraint, never across patients. Enforce in DB, not just UI.
pharmacy_privacy_patterns.audit_logging: Every PHI access logged: user_id, action, timestamp, IP. Required for HIPAA-ish compliance.
pharmacy_privacy_patterns.data_minimization: Do not store more than necessary. Prescription numbers, medication names, refill counts. No full medical history unless explicitly scoped.

e_paper_optimization.dithering_method: Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion (best quality for photographic content) or Bayer matrix (best for structured graphics/icons)
e_paper_optimization.color_depth: 1-bit (pure black/white) or 4-bit grayscale (16 shades) for standard e-ink; Spectra 6-color for color e-ink

recommended_pipeline.step_1: Design web version at full color (standard CSS/Tailwind)
recommended_pipeline.step_2: Build-time image processing: Sharp (Node.js) applies contrast +20%, sharpening, then dithering
recommended_pipeline.step_4: Astro component detects output target via build flag: `EPAPER=true astro build`
recommended_pipeline.step_5: E-paper tile layout uses CSS Grid with fixed tile dimensions matching display resolution
recommended_pipeline.implementation: Sharp + custom Astro integration. Sharp supports Floyd-Steinberg natively in toBuffer({dither: 1.0}).

layout_rules.typography: High contrast only — black text on white, minimum 18px/14pt. No gray text.
layout_rules.images: Pre-dithered at build time. Avoid gradients — use flat fills.
layout_rules.animation: None. E-paper refresh rate (even Modos at 75Hz) causes ghosting with CSS transitions.
layout_rules.grid: Fixed pixel grids matching display resolution (common: 800x600, 1024x758, 1872x1404)
layout_rules.responsive_dual: Use CSS media query @media (display-mode: browser) for web vs build-flag for e-paper compile target

tools: custom Astro integration for build-time target switching
e_paper_optimization.2026_note: Modos Paper Monitor (75Hz e-ink) enables dynamic mode switching — text in 1-bit, images in 4-bit grayscale, simultaneously. FPGA-based, C API.
